definitions.name: \mathcal I_i^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)
definitions.construction:
For \(i\in[H]\), define the internally constructed coalitionwise relaxation
\[
 \mathcal I_i^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)
 =\left[
 \sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}\omega_H(C)
 \left\{\inf_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}g_C(q)
       -\sup_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}g_{C\cup\{i\}}(q)\right\},
 \sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}\omega_H(C)
 \left\{\sup_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}g_C(q)
       -\inf_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}g_{C\cup\{i\}}(q)\right\}
 \right].
\]
Thus every distinct coalition return is optimized over its own copy of the posterior fiber before the signed Shapley sum is formed.  This relaxation is defined internally for comparison; its definition does not attribute this operation to an external estimator or workflow.

definitions.name: \mathfrak G_{\varepsilon}
definitions.construction: For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), \(\mathfrak G_{\varepsilon}\) is the primitive tuple \(H=2\), \(\mathcal S=\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), \(S_1=0\), \(\tau=(0,0,0,0,0)\), \(K_t(y\mid s,a)=1/2\) for every \(t,s,a,y\), \(r_1((s,a),y)=0\), \(r_2((s,a),y)=y\), and \(i=1\). For every state and time, \(\pi_t(0\mid s)=1\). For both states, \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(1\mid s)=\varepsilon\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(0\mid s)=1-\varepsilon\), and \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},2}(1\mid s)=1\).

definitions.name: [L_i^{\alpha},U_i^{\alpha}]
definitions.construction: \(L_i^{\alpha}=\inf_{K'\in\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K):\,K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)>0\ \forall t}L_i(K',\tau)\) and \(U_i^{\alpha}=\sup_{K'\in\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K):\,K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)>0\ \forall t}U_i(K',\tau)\), with closure in posterior-row space when a confidence fiber approaches a zero factual cell.

definitions.name: \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M(K):R_t(x)\text{ and }R_t(x')\text{ are independent for all }t\in[H]\text{ and distinct }x,x'\in\mathcal X\}\).

definitions.name: \Theta_i^{\mathrm{CI}}(K,\tau)
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_i^{\mathrm{CI}}(K,\tau)=\{\Phi_i(\mathcal M\mid\tau):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)\}\), with the selected posterior kernel \(q_{t,x_t}^{\mathrm{CI}}=\delta_{y_t}\) and \(q_{t,x}^{\mathrm{CI}}=K_t(\cdot\mid x)\) for \(x\ne x_t\).

definitions.name: \mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)
definitions.construction:
Work on the fixed discrete stratum \(H=2\), \(\mathcal S=\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), \(\tau=(0,0,0,0,0)\), and \(i=1\).  Write \(\theta=(K,r,\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}})\).  The interior center \(\theta^\star\) has \(K_t(y\mid s,a)=1/2\) for all cells, \(r_1((s,a),y)=0\), \(r_2((s,a),y)=y\), \(\pi_t(1\mid s)=1/64\) for every \(t,s\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(1\mid s)=1/4\), and \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},2}(1\mid s)=63/64\) for every \(s\).  All complementary action probabilities are determined by normalization.  Set \(\rho=1/1024\) and, with probability vectors ordered by \(0,1\), set
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_{\mathrm{pr}}(\theta,\theta^\star)=\max\Bigl\{
&\max_{t,x}\|K_t(\cdot\mid x)-(1/2,1/2)\|_1,
 \max_{x,y}|r_1(x,y)|,
 \max_{x,y}|r_2(x,y)-y|,\\
&\max_{t,s}\|\pi_t(\cdot\mid s)-(63/64,1/64)\|_1,\\
&\max_s\|\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(\cdot\mid s)-(3/4,1/4)\|_1,
 \max_s\|\pi_{\mathrm{base},2}(\cdot\mid s)-(1/64,63/64)\|_1
\Bigr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Define \(\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\) to be the set of all valid kernel, reward, and policy primitives on this stratum satisfying \(d_{\mathrm{pr}}(\theta,\theta^\star)<\rho\).  Apart from the probability-simplex constraints, no continuous cell is held fixed.  For \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\), define
\[
 \mu_\tau(\theta)=\prod_{t=1}^2\pi_t(0\mid0)K_t(0\mid(0,0)),
\]
\[
 s_\pi(\theta)=\min_{t,s,a}\min\{\pi_t(a\mid s),\pi_{\mathrm{base},t}(a\mid s)\},
 \qquad
 s_K(\theta)=\min_{t,x,y}K_t(y\mid x),
\]
\[
 V_{\mathrm{fd}}(\theta)=\min_{x\in\mathcal X}
 \operatorname{Var}_{Y\sim K_2(\cdot\mid x)}\{r_2(x,Y)\},
\]
and the lower and upper excess widths of the internal relaxation by
\[
 \Delta_1^-(\theta)=L_1(K,\tau)-\inf\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau),
 \qquad
 \Delta_1^+(\theta)=\sup\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)-U_1(K,\tau).
\]

statements.statement: For every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M(K)\), conditioning on \(\tau\) induces a kernel \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\). Conversely, every \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\) is induced by one compatible response-table law \(\lambda_t\) at each time, shared by all nonfactual rows and all coalition worlds; the timewise laws can be sampled independently to form a member of \(\mathfrak M(K)\).
statements.justification: This is the exact bridge from arbitrary within-time response coupling to an evaluable posterior Markov kernel.
statements.gap: Lally, Kazemi, and Paoletti prove simultaneous one-step row realization; this lemma specializes that construction to the operational policy-switching worlds and makes the common-law requirement explicit.
statements.consumer: The sharpness theorem and compiler can optimize posterior rows without enumerating full response tables.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(t\in[H]\), and abbreviate \(E_t=\{R_t(x_t)=y_t\}\).  By \(\text{ass:transition-marginals}\), \(\Pr(E_t)=K_t(y_t\mid x_t)=p_t\), which is positive by \(\text{ass:factual-positivity}\).  For a compatible SCM define
\[
 q_{t,x}(y)=\Pr\{R_t(x)=y\mid E_t\}.
\]
Then \(q_{t,x_t}=\delta_{y_t}\).  If \(x\ne x_t\), the multiplication rule and monotonicity of probability give, for every \(y\in\mathcal S\),
\[
 p_tq_{t,x}(y)
 =\Pr\{R_t(x_t)=y_t,R_t(x)=y\}
 \le \Pr\{R_t(x)=y\}
 =K_t(y\mid x),
\]
where the last equality is \(\text{ass:transition-marginals}\).  Thus the induced array belongs to \(\mathcal B(K,\tau)\) by \(\text{def:posterior-row-fiber}\).

Conversely, fix \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\).  At time \(t\), first draw a variable \(F_t\) with law \(K_t(\cdot\mid x_t)\), and put \(R_t(x_t)=F_t\).  Suppose first that \(p_t<1\).  For every \(x\ne x_t\), define
\[
 h_{t,x}(y)=\frac{K_t(y\mid x)-p_tq_{t,x}(y)}{1-p_t}.
\]
The numerator is nonnegative by \(\text{def:posterior-row-fiber}\), and
\[
 \sum_{y\in\mathcal S}h_{t,x}(y)
 =\frac{1-p_t}{1-p_t}=1.
\]
Conditional on \(F_t=y_t\), draw the coordinates \(R_t(x)\), \(x\ne x_t\), independently with respective laws \(q_{t,x}\).  Conditional on \(F_t\ne y_t\), draw them independently with respective laws \(h_{t,x}\).  The particular value of \(F_t\ne y_t\) need not enter this second draw.  For every nonfactual row,
\[
 \Pr\{R_t(x)=y\}
 =p_tq_{t,x}(y)+(1-p_t)h_{t,x}(y)
 =K_t(y\mid x).
\]
If \(p_t=1\), the inequalities \(q_{t,x}(y)\le K_t(y\mid x)\), together with equality of both coordinate sums to one, imply \(q_{t,x}=K_t(\cdot\mid x)\); use that law in the only, factual branch and omit the residual branch.  In either case the resulting random table has a law \(\lambda_t\) with all the required marginals and with conditional row marginals \(q_{t,x}\) given \(E_t\).  Notice that this is one joint table law: it is not reselected by a coalition or by the row later queried.

Sample the constructed tables independently over \(t\).  This enforces \(\text{ass:independent-time-disturbances}\), while table lookup supplies the equations in \(\text{ass:markov-structural-equations}\); the displayed marginal calculation supplies \(\text{ass:transition-marginals}\).  Hence the construction is in \(\mathfrak M(K)\) by \(\text{def:compatible-scm-class}\).  Because the events \(E_t\) belong to independent time blocks,
\[
 \Pr\{R_1\in dr_1,\ldots,R_H\in dr_H\mid E_1\cap\cdots\cap E_H\}
 =\prod_{t=1}^H\Pr\{R_t\in dr_t\mid E_t\}.
\]
Under the specified policy interventions, initial-state and action-randomization factors are fixed and do not alter these environment-table likelihoods.  A counterfactual path at time \(t\) queries exactly the coordinate \(R_t(S_t,A_t)\); earlier states are functions of earlier, conditionally independent blocks.  Its conditional transition law is therefore \(q_{t,S_t,A_t}\).  Thus every coalition world is evaluated by the same posterior Markov kernel \(q\), completing both directions.

statements.statement: For every \(i\in[H]\), \(\Theta_i(K,\tau)=[L_i(K,\tau),U_i(K,\tau)]\). Both endpoints are attained by compatible SCMs in \(\mathfrak M(K)\). Each endpoint has a witness whose posterior row \(q_{t,x}\) is a vertex of its capped-simplex factor for every \(t\in[H]\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\), and the witness is returned as a compact conditional response-table sampler rather than an exponentially long mass table.
statements.justification: This identifies exactly what transition marginals determine about one trajectory credit coordinate when no cross-row coupling is selected.
statements.gap: Lee, Plecko, and Bareinboim give generic Layer-3 Shapley extrema and Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim give generic canonical-SCM bounds; neither gives this posterior row product, interval image, or compact sequential endpoint witness.
statements.consumer: A \(\phi\)-PPO reward or critic update can distinguish robustly signed credit from credit whose sign depends on an unobserved response coupling.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\text{def:posterior-row-fiber}\), the choice \(q_{t,x}=K_t(\cdot\mid x)\) for \(x\ne x_t\), together with \(q_{t,x_t}=\delta_{y_t}\), is feasible because \(0<p_t\le1\).  Hence \(\mathcal B(K,\tau)\) is nonempty.  Each of its nonfactual row factors is the intersection of a finite-dimensional simplex with finitely many closed half-spaces, so it is compact and convex; the full finite product has the same properties.

For a fixed coalition, finite-state Markov expansion expresses \(g_C(q)\) as a finite sum of path terms, each term being a known reward times policy probabilities and one coordinate of \(q\) at each time.  Consequently \(g_C\), and hence \(\Phi_i\) by \(\text{def:shapley-coordinate}\), is a continuous polynomial.  The two directions of \(\text{lem:posterior-row-projection}\) now give the equality of sets
\[
 \Theta_i(K,\tau)=\{\Phi_i(q):q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\}.
\]
Compactness and continuity give minimizers \(q^-\) and maximizers \(q^+\), whose values are \(L_i(K,\tau)\) and \(U_i(K,\tau)\) by \(\text{def:shared-endpoints}\).

For \(s\in[0,1]\), convexity makes \(q(s)=(1-s)q^-+sq^+\) feasible, and \(f(s)=\Phi_i(q(s))\) is continuous.  For completeness, the intermediate-value step follows by bisection: for any \(c\) between \(f(0)\) and \(f(1)\), repeatedly retain a half-interval whose endpoint values bracket \(c\).  The nested intervals have lengths tending to zero and hence a common point \(s_*\); continuity excludes \(f(s_*)<c\) and \(f(s_*)>c\), so \(f(s_*)=c\).  Therefore the displayed image is the whole interval \([L_i,U_i]\), not merely a set with those extrema.  Applying the converse construction in \(\text{lem:posterior-row-projection}\) to \(q^-\), \(q^+\), or \(q(s_*)\) produces compatible SCMs.  In particular both endpoints are attained without introducing a time-common mixture variable.

It remains to obtain vertex witnesses.  In every path monomial, at a fixed time \(t\) exactly one transition row is queried.  Thus, with all other rows fixed, every \(g_C(q)\), and consequently \(\Phi_i(q)\), is affine in any one row \(q_{t,x}\).  Start from an endpoint optimizer and consider one row factor.  Its current row must optimize the resulting affine functional conditionally on all other rows, since otherwise replacing that row would improve the global endpoint.  An affine functional on a polytope has a vertex optimizer: if an optimizing point is not extreme, write it as a nontrivial convex combination; at least one component is no worse, and repeating inside the proper optimizing face terminates after finitely many dimension reductions at a vertex.  Replace the row by such a vertex.  Iterating over the finitely many \((t,x)\) preserves the endpoint value and makes every row a vertex; the factual singleton rows are already vertices.

Finally, the construction in \(\text{lem:posterior-row-projection}\) is a compact sampler.  At each time it stores \(K_t(\cdot\mid x_t)\), the selected conditional rows \(q_{t,x}\), and, when \(p_t<1\), the residual rows \(h_{t,x}\).  It then samples the factual coordinate followed by conditionally independent remaining coordinates.  This uses \(O(H|\mathcal X||\mathcal S|)\) displayed probabilities and need not list the generally exponential mass table on \(\mathcal S^{\mathcal X}\).

statements.statement: For every \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\), \(P_i(z,q)\) has degree at most \(H-1\) in \(z\), and \(\Phi_i(q)=\int_0^1P_i(z,q)\,dz=\sum_{j=1}^H\nu_jP_i(\zeta_j,q)\). For fixed \(q\), all terms are evaluated exactly in \(O(H^2|\mathcal S|^2|\mathcal A|)\) arithmetic operations, without enumerating coalitions or state paths.
statements.justification: The exact Shapley sum must be compressed before the shared endpoint optimization can be computationally meaningful.
statements.gap: Witter et al. compress do-Shapley by graph classes, while Theorem 4.2 of Li, Lee, and Bareinboim gives an optimal coalition proposal and sample guarantee; this proposition gives an exact Markov polynomial representation but does not claim the beta-integral identity itself as novel.
statements.consumer: It supplies the polynomial-size arithmetic input for exact shared-SCM endpoint compilation.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\), and let \(m=H-1\).  Under the definition of \(G_i^b(z,q)\), each \(t\ne i\) independently selects \(\alpha_t^1\) with probability \(z\) and \(\alpha_t^0\) with probability \(1-z\), while membership of \(i\) is fixed at \(b\).  Expanding these independent selections and using \(\text{def:coalition-policy}\) gives
\[
 G_i^0(z,q)=\sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}
 z^{|C|}(1-z)^{m-|C|}g_C(q),
\]
\[
 G_i^1(z,q)=\sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}
 z^{|C|}(1-z)^{m-|C|}g_{C\cup\{i\}}(q).
\]
Their difference \(P_i(z,q)\) is therefore a polynomial of degree at most \(m=H-1\).  Repeated integration by parts, with the boundary cases at zero and one, gives for \(0\le k\le m\)
\[
 \int_0^1 z^k(1-z)^{m-k}\,dz
 =\frac{k!(m-k)!}{(m+1)!}.
\]
Integrating the finite expansion term by term and invoking \(\text{def:shapley-coordinate}\) yields
\[
 \int_0^1P_i(z,q)\,dz
 =\sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}
 \omega_H(C)\{g_C(q)-g_{C\cup\{i\}}(q)\}
 =\Phi_i(q).
\]

The \(H\) pairwise distinct nodes \(\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_H\) interpolate every polynomial of degree at most \(H-1\): explicitly,
\[
 P_i(z,q)=\sum_{j=1}^H P_i(\zeta_j,q)\ell_j(z).
\]
After integration, the definition \(\nu_j=\int_0^1\ell_j(z)\,dz\) gives
\[
 \Phi_i(q)=\sum_{j=1}^H\nu_jP_i(\zeta_j,q)=\mathsf Q_i(q),
\]
which is \(\text{def:quadrature-representation}\).  This includes \(H=1\), when both sides are the constant marginal contribution.

For one fixed \(z\) and branch \(b\), forward recursion keeps the current state distribution and, at every time, sums over \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), and \(y\in\mathcal S\).  It therefore uses \(O(H|\mathcal S|^2|\mathcal A|)\) arithmetic operations and sums rewards during the same recursion.  There are two branches at each of \(H\) nodes, so all values in the last display cost \(O(H^2|\mathcal S|^2|\mathcal A|)\) operations.  No coalition or state-path list is formed.

statements.justification: This affine identity turns every signed reward and quadrature coefficient into a concrete nonnegative objective without changing the shared posterior kernel.
statements.gap: Generic marginal-MAP formulations permit nonnegative factors but do not provide this reward-range normalization and endpoint recovery identity for the signed trajectory-Shapley polynomial.
statements.consumer: The compiler question receives two explicit nonnegative objectives whose maximizers still represent one shared SCM per endpoint.
statements.proof_tex:
For each \(t\), \(M_t-m_t\ge0\).  If \(R=\sum_t(M_t-m_t)=0\), every summand vanishes, so \(r_t(x,y)=m_t=M_t\) for all \(x,y\).  Every coalition return is then the same constant \(\sum_tm_t\).  The signed differences in \(\text{def:shapley-coordinate}\) vanish, and \(L_i=U_i=0\) by \(\text{def:shared-endpoints}\).

Assume henceforth that \(R>0\).  On any complete path with total reward \(G'=\sum_tr_t((s'_t,a'_t),s'_{t+1})\), the definitions give
\[
 \sum_{t=1}^Hh_t^+=\frac{G'-\sum_tm_t}{R},\qquad
 \sum_{t=1}^Hh_t^-=\frac{\sum_tM_t-G'}{R}.
\]
The stagewise bounds \(m_t\le r_t\le M_t\) imply that the first quantity lies in \([0,1]\), and since \(R=\sum_tM_t-\sum_tm_t\), the second equals one minus the first.  Taking the Markov expectation in branch \((j,b)\) proves
\[
 0\le h_{jb}(q)\le1,
 \qquad
 h_{jb}(q)=\frac{G_i^b(\zeta_j,q)-\sum_tm_t}{R}.
\]

For a real number \(a\), the summand used in \(F_i^\sigma\) is \(ah\) if \(a\ge0\), and \(|a|(1-h)=|a|+ah\) if \(a<0\).  For each \(j\), the two coefficients \(a_{j0}^\sigma=\sigma\nu_j\) and \(a_{j1}^\sigma=-\sigma\nu_j\) have total negative-part magnitude \(|\nu_j|\).  Therefore \(\text{def:nonnegative-endpoint-objectives}\) implies
\[
\begin{aligned}
 F_i^\sigma(q)
 &=C_\nu+\sum_{j=1}^H\sum_{b=0}^1a_{jb}^\sigma h_{jb}(q)\\
 &=C_\nu+\frac{\sigma}{R}\sum_{j=1}^H\nu_j
       \{G_i^0(\zeta_j,q)-G_i^1(\zeta_j,q)\}\\
 &=C_\nu+\frac{\sigma}{R}\Phi_i(q),
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last equality is \(\text{prop:exact-coalition-compression}\).  All terms in the defining expression of \(F_i^\sigma\) are nonnegative because \(0\le h_{jb}\le1\).  Maximizing the identity over the same set \(\mathcal B(K,\tau)\) gives
\[
 V_{+1}=C_\nu+\frac{U_i}{R},\qquad
 V_{-1}=C_\nu-\frac{L_i}{R},
\]
and rearrangement proves the two endpoint formulas.

statements.statement: For every \(0<\varepsilon<1\), in \(\mathfrak G_{\varepsilon}\) write \(u=q_{1,(0,1)}(1)\), \(w=q_{2,(0,1)}(1)\), \(z=q_{2,(1,0)}(1)\), and \(v=q_{2,(1,1)}(1)\). The posterior fiber makes \(u,w,z,v\) independently range over \([0,1]\), while \(q_{t,(0,0)}=\delta_0\). Direct recursion gives \(g_{\varnothing}=0\), \(g_{\{1\}}=\varepsilon uz\), \(g_{\{2\}}=w\), and \(g_{\{1,2\}}=(1-\varepsilon u)w+\varepsilon uv\), so \(\Phi_1=(\varepsilon u/2)(w-z-v)\). Thus \(U_1=\varepsilon/2\) is attained at \((u,w,z,v)=(1,1,0,0)\), and \(L_1=-\varepsilon\) is attained at \((1,0,1,1)\). With independent coalition copies, \(g_{\varnothing}\in\{0\}\), \(g_{\{1\}}\in[0,\varepsilon]\), \(g_{\{2\}}\in[0,1]\), and \(g_{\{1,2\}}\in[0,1]\), whence \(\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}=[-(1+\varepsilon)/2,1/2]\). Its lower and upper excess widths over the shared interval both equal \((1-\varepsilon)/2>0\). At \(\varepsilon=1/4\), continuity of extrema over compact continuously varying fibers yields a relative neighborhood of the full primitive tuple, restricted to positive factual cells and valid probability simplices and containing interior policy points, on which both slacks remain positive.
statements.justification: The theorem separates sharp optimization over one common SCM from a deliberately internal relaxation and certifies that the separation persists on a quantitatively nondegenerate open family.
statements.gap: Published trajectory-credit procedures considered here do not use coalitionwise ambiguity optimization; the relevant mathematical gap is whether separate coalition extrema can nevertheless serve as a sharp surrogate for one shared-SCM Shapley coordinate.
statements.consumer: The result prevents the internal interval-arithmetic relaxation from being reported as sharp trajectory-conditioned mean credit in \(\phi\)-PPO reward or critic updates; it makes no claim about PTR's RMS priority.
statements.proof_tex:
In \(\mathfrak G_\varepsilon\), \(p_t=1/2\) for both times.  For a binary nonfactual row whose observed marginal is \((1/2,1/2)\), \(\texttt{def:posterior-row-fiber}\) imposes
\[
 \frac12q(0)\le\frac12,
 \qquad
 \frac12q(1)\le\frac12,
 \qquad
 q(0)+q(1)=1,
\]
which is exactly \(0\le q(1)\le1\).  Because the fiber is a Cartesian product of row factors, \(u,w,z,v\) range independently over \([0,1]\), and the factual rows equal \(\delta_0\).

The first-stage reward is zero and the second-stage reward is the terminal next state.  Under the empty coalition both factual rows are queried, so \(g_\varnothing=0\).  Under \(\{1\}\), the time-one baseline chooses action one with probability \(\varepsilon\), reaches state one with conditional probability \(u\), and the retained time-two policy then uses action zero, whose success probability is \(z\).  Hence
\[
 g_{\{1\}}=\varepsilon uz.
\]
Under \(\{2\}\), time one remains factual and time two takes action one at state zero, giving
\[
 g_{\{2\}}=w.
\]
Under \(\{1,2\}\), the time-one baseline reaches state one with probability \(\varepsilon u\).  The time-two baseline success probability is \(w\) from state zero and \(v\) from state one.  Therefore
\[
 g_{\{1,2\}}=(1-\varepsilon u)w+\varepsilon uv.
\]
For \(H=2\), both Shapley weights are \(1/2\).  Substitution into \(\texttt{def:shapley-coordinate}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Phi_1(q)
 &=\frac12\{g_\varnothing-g_{\{1\}}+g_{\{2\}}-g_{\{1,2\}}\}\\
 &=\frac{\varepsilon u}{2}(w-z-v).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(u,w,z,v\in[0,1]\), the maximum is \(\varepsilon/2\), attained at \((u,w,z,v)=(1,1,0,0)\), and the minimum is \(-\varepsilon\), attained at \((1,0,1,1)\).  The equality with \([L_1,U_1]\), together with compatible-SCM attainment by these common row assignments, follows from \(\texttt{thm:sharp-shared-interval}\).

The internally defined relaxation assigns a separate posterior-kernel copy to each distinct coalition return.  The displayed recursions imply
\[
 g_\varnothing\in\{0\},
 \qquad
 g_{\{1\}}\in[0,\varepsilon],
 \qquad
 g_{\{2\}}\in[0,1],
 \qquad
 g_{\{1,2\}}\in[0,1].
\]
Each endpoint is attained by a suitable row assignment in its own copy.  The explicit interval formula in \(\texttt{def:independent-coalition-outer-bound}\) consequently gives
\[
 \mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)
 =\left[-\frac{1+\varepsilon}{2},\frac12\right].
\]
Its lower excess below \(-\varepsilon\) and upper excess above \(\varepsilon/2\) both equal
\[
 \frac{1-\varepsilon}{2}>0.
\]

We prove the neighborhood assertion rather than infer it from the single tuple.  On the fixed discrete stratum, restrict first to a sufficiently small relative neighborhood on which both factual transition cells remain positive.  If \(K'\) approaches \(K\) in maximum rowwise \(\ell^1\) distance and their factual cells have a common positive lower bound, truncate each old feasible posterior row at the new caps \(K'_t(y\mid x)/p'_t\) and redistribute the removed mass into unused cap capacity.  Exactly as in the row-matching calculation in \(\texttt{thm:quantitative-gap-neighborhood}\), the removed mass tends uniformly to zero.  Reversing \(K,K'\) proves Hausdorff convergence of the finite product fibers.

Every coalition return is a finite polynomial in the posterior rows, rewards, and policy probabilities, hence is uniformly continuous on a compact neighborhood of the valid primitive and posterior-row products.  Given Hausdorff-close fibers, match a maximizer or minimizer in either direction and apply this uniform continuity.  Thus each shared endpoint and each coalition-return extremum in the internal relaxation is continuous.  The two excess-width functions are finite sums and differences of these continuous extrema.  At \(\varepsilon=1/4\), both equal \(3/8\), so the set on which both are positive is a relative-open neighborhood of the displayed primitive tuple.

This neighborhood genuinely contains interior-policy points.  More explicitly, keep \(K,r\), and the time-one baseline at their \(\varepsilon=1/4\) values, and for \(0\le c\le1/64\) set \(\pi_t(1\mid s)=c\) and \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},2}(1\mid s)=1-c\) for all \(t,s\).  The same recursion, now with \(\eta=c\) and \(\beta=1-c\), gives
\[
 [L_1,U_1]=\left[-\frac14,\frac{1-c}{8}\right],
\]
\[
 \mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}
 =\left[-\frac58+\frac{3c}{8},\frac{1-c}{2}\right].
\]
The lower and upper excess widths are respectively \(3(1-c)/8\) and \(3(1-c)/8\), so the whole segment remains in the positive-gap set, and every point with \(c>0\) has all policy cells positive.  At \(c=1/64\) this point is \(\theta^\star\), and \(\texttt{thm:quantitative-gap-neighborhood}\) further supplies the explicit radius \(\rho=1/1024\), factual-region mass, support, variance, and uniform \(1/4\)-gap certificate under perturbations of every continuous primitive.  This proves the stated open-neighborhood conclusion and its quantitative strengthening.

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K)\) has simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\alpha\), then with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), \([L_i(K,\tau),U_i(K,\tau)]\subseteq[L_i^{\alpha},U_i^{\alpha}]\) simultaneously for every \(i\in[H]\) and every prespecified positive-probability factual trajectory and policy pair. On every realized confidence region whose rowwise polytopes are nonempty and for which each factual confidence row attains a positive value of \(K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)\), the confidence posterior-row fiber is a product of explicit local polytopes when every factual confidence-cell minimum is positive; when the minimum at time \(t\) is zero, the closure of that time block is the product, over its nonfactual rows, of simplices supported on next states having positive attainable marginal probability.
statements.justification: One confidence event must cover the entire vector of identified coordinate intervals after optimization, including boundary fibers.
statements.gap: Lally et al. take transition probabilities as known, while Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye treat general moment projections; neither gives this exact posterior-row fiber or whole-vector shared-SCM containment.
statements.consumer: Offline \(\phi\)-PPO analyses can report sampling-valid ambiguity bands for every mean credit used in reward and critic targets.
statements.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 \mathcal E=\{K\in\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K)\}.
\]
The assumed simultaneous coverage gives \(\Pr_K(\mathcal E)\ge1-\alpha\) under \(\text{ass:fixed-row-multinomial-sampling}\).  On \(\mathcal E\), every prespecified trajectory having positive probability under \(K\) makes the true kernel admissible in the defining optimizations for \(L_i^\alpha\) and \(U_i^\alpha\).  Hence, directly from \(\text{def:confidence-fiber-endpoints}\),
\[
 L_i^\alpha\le L_i(K,\tau)\le U_i(K,\tau)\le U_i^\alpha.
\]
The event \(\mathcal E\) depends only on the transition kernel, not on \(i\), \(\tau\), or the specified policy pair.  The same event therefore proves all asserted containments simultaneously; no additional union bound over queries is needed.  By \(\text{thm:sharp-shared-interval}\), these are containments of the whole population identified sets, not merely of selected point values.

For the geometric assertion, write the rowwise product confidence region as \(\prod_{t,x}\mathcal C_{t,x}\), and set
\[
 p_t^- =\min_{k\in\mathcal C_{t,x_t}}k(y_t),
 \qquad
 p_t^+ =\max_{k\in\mathcal C_{t,x_t}}k(y_t).
\]
The proposed statement assumes that the row polytopes are nonempty and that \(p_t^+>0\) for every \(t\), precisely the conditions needed for a nonempty positive-evidence confidence fiber.  If \(p_t^->0\), define, for \(x\ne x_t\),
\[
 \mathcal Q_{t,x}
 =\{q_x\in\Delta(\mathcal S):
       \exists k_x\in\mathcal C_{t,x}\text{ such that }
       p_t^-q_x(y)\le k_x(y)\text{ for all }y\}.
\]
This is the projection of an explicitly given bounded polyhedron in \((q_x,k_x)\), hence is an explicit polytope.  If \(q_x\) is feasible for some common factual probability \(p_t\ge p_t^-\), it is feasible at \(p_t^-\) with the same \(k_x\).  Conversely, choose a factual confidence row attaining \(p_t^-\) and, independently for each alternate row, a witnessing \(k_x\).  Product structure of the confidence region then supplies a single kernel \(K'\), with the same \(p_t^-\) for every alternate row.  Thus the union of posterior fibers is exactly
\[
 \{q_{t,x_t}=\delta_{y_t}\}\times
 \prod_{x\ne x_t}\mathcal Q_{t,x}
\]
at time \(t\), and the product over times is exact as well.

Suppose instead that \(p_t^-=0<p_t^+\), and put
\[
 J_{t,x}=\{y\in\mathcal S:\exists k\in\mathcal C_{t,x}
                    \text{ with }k(y)>0\}.
\]
For every positive factual value \(p\), feasibility \(pq_x(y)\le k_x(y)\) forces \(q_x(y)=0\) when \(y\notin J_{t,x}\).  This proves that the closure is contained in the simplex supported on \(J_{t,x}\).  Conversely, by convexity of \(\mathcal C_{t,x}\), averaging one witness for each member of the finite set \(J_{t,x}\) gives a single \(k_x^*\in\mathcal C_{t,x}\) positive on all of \(J_{t,x}\).  For any \(q_x\) supported there, all inequalities \(pq_x(y)\le k_x^*(y)\) hold for sufficiently small \(p>0\).  There are finitely many alternate rows, so one sufficiently small \(p\) works for all of them.  The projection of the convex factual-row polytope onto its \(y_t\)-coordinate is the interval \([0,p_t^+]\), so that common positive \(p\) is attainable.  Letting \(p\downarrow0\) proves that the closure is the claimed product of support simplices.  The same reasoning independently at each time completes the product-fiber characterization.

If \(p_t^+=0\), the set of confidence kernels satisfying the positive-evidence restriction is empty at that time, and its closure is empty rather than a support simplex.  This explicit countercase is why the positive-maximum clause in the proposed statement is necessary.

statements.statement: For two kernels \(K\) and \(K'\) with \(K_t(y_t\mid x_t)\ge\kappa\) and \(K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)\ge\kappa\) for every \(t\in[H]\), \(\max\{|L_i(K,\tau)-L_i(K',\tau)|,|U_i(K,\tau)-U_i(K',\tau)|\}\le 4DH\delta(K,K')/\kappa\). Consequently, plug-in and shrinking confidence-fiber endpoints are uniformly consistent on classes with \(\kappa\)-positive factual cells whenever \(\delta(\widehat K,K)\) converges uniformly to zero.
statements.justification: The stability price of trajectory conditioning should accumulate locally in time rather than divide by the full trajectory probability.
statements.gap: Existing compatible-MDP bounds do not provide an endpoint perturbation theorem under estimated transitions, and generic optimization continuity does not yield the explicit local denominator.
statements.consumer: The bound converts transition-row estimation error into an interpretable error guarantee for robust mean-credit updates.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(\delta=\delta(K,K')\), \(p=K_t(y_t\mid x_t)\), and \(p'=K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)\).  Then \(|p-p'|\le\delta\), and by hypothesis \(p,p'\ge\kappa\).  Fix a nonfactual row \(x\ne x_t\), abbreviate \(k=K_t(\cdot\mid x)\), \(k'=K'_t(\cdot\mid x)\), and take \(q\) in its \(K\)-fiber.  Truncate it to
\[
 a(y)=\min\{q(y),k'(y)/p'\},
 \qquad d_0=1-\sum_ya(y).
\]
Since \(pq(y)\le k(y)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 d_0
 &=\frac1{p'}\sum_y\bigl(p'q(y)-k'(y)\bigr)_+\\
 &\le\frac{|p'-p|+\|k-k'\|_1}{p'}
 \le\frac{2\delta}{\kappa}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, coordinatewise \(p'q-k'=(p'-p)q+(pq-k)+(k-k')\), the middle term is nonpositive, the positive parts of the first term sum to at most \(|p'-p|\sum_yq(y)\), and those of the last sum to at most \(\|k-k'\|_1\).

The remaining upper-cap capacity is
\[
 \sum_y\{k'(y)/p'-a(y)\}=1/p'-1+d_0\ge d_0.
\]
Redistribute mass \(d_0\) within these capacities to obtain \(q'\in\Delta(\mathcal S)\) satisfying \(p'q'(y)\le k'(y)\).  Removed and added masses are both \(d_0\), so
\[
 \|q-q'\|_1\le2d_0\le\frac{4\delta}{\kappa},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{TV}(q,q')\le\frac{2\delta}{\kappa}.
\]
The factual posterior rows agree exactly at \(\delta_{y_t}\).  Applying the construction to every row and time maps any \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\) to a \(q'\in\mathcal B(K',\tau)\) with
\[
 \max_{t,x}\operatorname{TV}(q_{t,x},q'_{t,x})
 \le\frac{2\delta}{\kappa}.
\]
The same construction with \(K,K'\) reversed gives the other Hausdorff direction.

Fix a coalition policy.  Couple its two Markov paths sequentially by maximal coupling whenever their histories still agree.  Conditional on agreement through time \(t\), the probability of a mismatch at the next transition is at most \(2\delta/\kappa\); the action kernel is identical in the two models.  A union bound over \(H\) transitions yields path-law total variation at most \(2H\delta/\kappa\).  Every complete return lies in \([\underline G,\overline G]\), an interval of width \(D\), so the layer-cake identity after subtracting \(\underline G\), or directly the coupling inequality, gives
\[
 |g_C(q)-g_C(q')|\le\frac{2DH\delta}{\kappa}.
\]
The Shapley weights are nonnegative and sum to one: grouping by \(k=|C|\),
\[
 \sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}\omega_H(C)
 =\sum_{k=0}^{H-1}{H-1\choose k}\frac{k!(H-k-1)!}{H!}=1.
\]
Consequently
\[
 |\Phi_i(q)-\Phi_i(q')|
 \le\sum_C\omega_H(C)
   \bigl(|g_C(q)-g_C(q')|+|g_{C\cup\{i\}}(q)-g_{C\cup\{i\}}(q')|\bigr)
 \le\frac{4DH\delta}{\kappa}.
\]

Match a maximizer over the \(K\)-fiber into the \(K'\)-fiber to obtain \(U_i(K,\tau)\le U_i(K',\tau)+4DH\delta/\kappa\), and reverse the kernels for the opposite inequality.  The identical two comparisons for minimizers prove the asserted bound for \(L_i\).  Attainment and the causal interpretation of these extrema are supplied by \(\text{thm:sharp-shared-interval}\).

For the consistency statement, let a class have true factual cells at least \(\kappa\) and suppose \(\delta(\widehat K,K)\to0\) uniformly in probability.  On the event \(\delta(\widehat K,K)<\kappa/2\), the empirical factual cells are at least \(\kappa/2\); applying the proved bound with positivity constant \(\kappa/2\) makes both plug-in endpoint errors tend uniformly to zero.  For a shrinking confidence fiber, assume its maximal row discrepancy from \(K\) tends uniformly to zero on its coverage event.  Eventually every member has factual cells at least \(\kappa/2\), and the same bound holds uniformly over every kernel in the fiber.  Taking its infimum and supremum therefore makes the confidence-fiber endpoints converge uniformly to the population endpoints.

statements.statement: On \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)\), conditioning on \(\tau\) induces the unique posterior kernel \(q^{\mathrm{CI}}\), where \(q_{t,x_t}^{\mathrm{CI}}=\delta_{y_t}\) and \(q_{t,x}^{\mathrm{CI}}=K_t(\cdot\mid x)\) for every \(x\ne x_t\). Therefore \(\Theta_i^{\mathrm{CI}}(K,\tau)=\{\Phi_i(q^{\mathrm{CI}})\}\subseteq\Theta_i(K,\tau)\).
statements.justification: The counterfactually independent subclass must reproduce the published point selection while remaining a proper subset of the unrestricted identified set.
statements.gap: This is solely a fidelity and sanity reduction to Equation 7 under Assumption 3.3 of Li, Lee, and Bareinboim, not a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Implementations recover the published trajectory-credit input to \(\phi\)-PPO when users impose counterfactual independence, while unrestricted analyses retain the full interval.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)\).  At a time \(t\), \(\text{ass:within-time-row-independence}\) makes every \(R_t(x)\), \(x\ne x_t\), independent of the factual coordinate \(R_t(x_t)\).  Since \(p_t>0\), conditioning on \(R_t(x_t)=y_t\) therefore gives
\[
 \Pr\{R_t(x)=y\mid R_t(x_t)=y_t\}
 =\Pr\{R_t(x)=y\}=K_t(y\mid x)
\]
for \(x\ne x_t\), using \(\text{ass:transition-marginals}\) through \(\text{def:counterfactual-independent-subclass}\).  Consistency on the conditioned coordinate gives \(q_{t,x_t}=\delta_{y_t}\).  Independence across times, inherited from \(\mathfrak M(K)\), makes the full-trajectory posterior kernel uniquely equal to \(q^{\mathrm{CI}}\) in \(\text{def:counterfactual-independent-target}\).

This kernel is feasible in \(\mathcal B(K,\tau)\): for \(x\ne x_t\),
\[
 p_tq_{t,x}^{\mathrm{CI}}(y)=p_tK_t(y\mid x)\le K_t(y\mid x),
\]
and its factual row is the required point mass.  Every member of the counterfactually independent subclass therefore has the same Markov recursion and the same credit \(\Phi_i(q^{\mathrm{CI}})\), proving
\[
 \Theta_i^{\mathrm{CI}}(K,\tau)=\{\Phi_i(q^{\mathrm{CI}})\}.
\]
Because \(q^{\mathrm{CI}}\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\), \(\text{thm:sharp-shared-interval}\) gives \(\Phi_i(q^{\mathrm{CI}})\in\Theta_i(K,\tau)\), which proves the asserted subset relation.

statements.statement: For rational \(K\), \(r\), \(\pi\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{base}}\), and rational quadrature data with \(R>0\), \(\mathsf{Compile}_i\) has an explicit realization of each \(F_i^\sigma\), \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\), as a nonnegative finite factor circuit \(\mathfrak F_i^\sigma\) with one selector \(Z_{t,x}\) for each posterior row and no selector copies across quadrature, forced-membership, state-path, or reward-time branches.  Every legal order \(\preceq\) returns \(V_\sigma\) in \(O(H^2N d^{w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)+1})\) rational arithmetic operations.  Intermediate and output rational bit lengths are polynomial in the rational input length, \(N\), and the requested output precision.  The table \(\mathsf{BP}_\sigma\) backtracks one joint assignment of row vertices, and the gluing construction turns it into a compatible SCM attaining \(U_i=R(V_{+1}-C_\nu)\) or \(L_i=R(C_\nu-V_{-1})\), respectively.

For the objects in \(\texttt{def:quantitative-gap-neighborhood}\), the center \(\theta^\star\) obeys
\[
 [L_1(K,\tau),U_1(K,\tau)]=[-1/4,63/512],
 \qquad
 \mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)=[-317/512,63/128],
\]
so \(\Delta_1^-(\theta^\star)=\Delta_1^+(\theta^\star)=189/512\).  Let \(\kappa=511/1024\).  Every \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\) satisfies
\[
 K_t(0\mid(0,0))>\kappa,
 \qquad
 \mu_\tau(\theta)>left(\frac{63}{64}-\rho\right)^2
                         \left(\frac12-\rho\right)^2>\frac15,
\]
\[
 s_\pi(\theta)>\frac1{64}-\rho>\frac1{100},
 \qquad
 s_K(\theta)>\frac12-\rho>\frac25,
\]
\[
 V_{\mathrm{fd}}(\theta)>left(\frac14-\rho^2\right)(1-2\rho)^2>\frac15,
 \qquad
 \Delta_1^-(\theta)>\frac14,
 \qquad
 \Delta_1^+(\theta)>\frac14.
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\) is a relative-open, positive-mass family with uniformly interior policy and transition support, nonvanishing failure-driving conditional variance, and a uniform strict gap between the sharp shared-SCM interval and the internally defined coalitionwise relaxation.
statements.justification: This theorem supplies a quantitative generic-class certificate for the strictness of the internally defined relaxation, including positive region mass, support, conditional variance, perturbation radius, and failure magnitude.
statements.gap: A single boundary-policy tuple does not establish that shared-SCM incompatibility persists on a failure-relevant, statistically nondegenerate set of primitives.
statements.consumer: It certifies that separate coalition optimization can remain materially conservative for trajectory-conditioned mean-credit updates used by \(\phi\)-PPO even when every policy and transition cell is interior.
statements.proof_tex:
At \(\theta^\star\), every factual transition probability is \(1/2\).  By \(\texttt{def:posterior-row-fiber}\), a binary nonfactual posterior row with success probability \(a\) is constrained only by
\[
 \frac12a\le\frac12,
 \qquad
 \frac12(1-a)\le\frac12,
\]
and hence \(a\in[0,1]\).  The posterior fiber is a product, so the coordinates \(u,w,z,v\) range independently over \([0,1]\), whereas the two factual rows are \(\delta_0\).

Put \(\eta=1/64\), \(\beta=63/64\), and \(\epsilon=1/4\).  Since the first-stage reward is zero and the second-stage reward is the terminal state, direct Markov recursion gives
\[
 g_\varnothing=0,
 \qquad
 g_{\{1\}}=\epsilon u\{(1-\eta)z+\eta v\},
 \qquad
 g_{\{2\}}=\beta w,
\]
and
\[
 g_{\{1,2\}}=(1-\epsilon u)\beta w
 +\epsilon u\{(1-\beta)z+\beta v\}.
\]
Indeed, a switch at time one chooses action one with probability \(\epsilon\), reaches state one with probability \(u\), and then the retained policy mixes the rows \((1,0)\) and \((1,1)\) with probabilities \(1-\eta\) and \(\eta\).  A switch at time two mixes action one with probability \(\beta\), which proves each displayed term.

For \(H=2\), both Shapley weights are \(1/2\).  Since \(\beta+\eta=1\), substitution into \(\texttt{def:shapley-coordinate}\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Phi_1(q)
 &=\frac12\{g_\varnothing-g_{\{1\}}+g_{\{2\}}-g_{\{1,2\}}\}\\
 &=\frac{\epsilon u}{2}
 \left[\beta w-\{2-\beta-\eta\}z-(\beta+\eta)v\right]\\
 &=\frac{u}{8}\left(\frac{63}{64}w-z-v\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
All four variables lie in \([0,1]\).  Therefore the minimum is \(-1/4\), attained at \((u,w,z,v)=(1,0,1,1)\), and the maximum is \(63/512\), attained at \((1,1,0,0)\).  This proves the first shared-interval display by \(\texttt{def:shared-endpoints}\).

For the internal relaxation, the preceding recursion and nonnegativity give
\[
 \inf g_\varnothing=\sup g_\varnothing=0,
 \quad \inf g_{\{1\}}=0,
 \quad \sup g_{\{1\}}=\epsilon=\frac14,
 \quad \inf g_{\{2\}}=0,
 \quad \sup g_{\{2\}}=\beta=\frac{63}{64}.
\]
Moreover, \(g_{\{1,2\}}\ge0\), its minimum is zero, and its maximum is obtained by setting \(w=z=v=u=1\):
\[
 \sup g_{\{1,2\}}
 =\beta+\epsilon(1-\beta)
 =\frac{63}{64}+\frac1{256}
 =\frac{253}{256}.
\]
The explicit formula in \(\texttt{def:independent-coalition-outer-bound}\) now gives
\[
 \inf\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}
 =-\frac12\left(\frac14+\frac{253}{256}\right)
 =-\frac{317}{512},
 \qquad
 \sup\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}
 =\frac12\frac{63}{64}=\frac{63}{128}.
\]
Subtracting the shared endpoints gives
\[
 -\frac14-\left(-\frac{317}{512}\right)
 =\frac{63}{128}-\frac{63}{512}
 =\frac{189}{512}.
\]

We next prove a uniform perturbation bound.  Write the already defined center as \(\theta^\star=(K^\star,r^\star,\pi^\star,\pi_{\mathrm{base}}^\star)\), and fix \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\).  The metric definition implies
\[
 \delta(K,K^\star)<\rho,
 \qquad
 p_t=K_t(0\mid(0,0))>\frac12-\rho=\kappa,
\]
With the center rewards and policies held fixed, the complete return lies in \([0,1]\), so its range width is \(D=1\).  Applying \(\texttt{thm:local-positivity-modulus}\) with \(H=2\) therefore bounds the movement of either shared endpoint caused by changing \(K^\star\) to \(K\) by
\[
 \frac{4DH\rho}{\kappa}=\frac{8\rho}{\kappa}.
\]

Now hold \(K\), and hence its posterior fiber, fixed while changing the center rewards and policies to those of \(\theta\).  Under a maximal coupling, the action selected at either time differs with conditional probability at most one half of the relevant rowwise \(\ell^1\) distance, hence by less than \(\rho/2\).  A union bound over the two action times makes the complete path laws differ in total variation by less than \(\rho\); conditional on equal actions and states, the common posterior kernel gives equal next states.  The center total reward is in \([0,1]\), and the two stage rewards on any fixed path move by less than \(2\rho\).  Thus, for every coalition and every fixed feasible \(q\),
\[
 |g_C(q;\theta)-g_C(q;K,r^\star,\pi^\star,\pi_{\mathrm{base}}^\star)|
 <\rho+2\rho=3\rho.
\]
The Shapley weights are nonnegative and sum to one.  Each marginal contribution contains two coalition returns, so
\[
 |\Phi_1(q;\theta)-\Phi_1(q;K,r^\star,\pi^\star,\pi_{\mathrm{base}}^\star)|<6\rho.
\]
Taking minima or maxima over the unchanged fiber and combining the two perturbations shows that each shared endpoint moves from its value at \(\theta^\star\) by at most
\[
 A=\frac{8\rho}{\kappa}+6\rho.
\]

For completeness, the same constant controls each endpoint of the internal relaxation.  To see this without interchanging optimization operators, take a row \(q\) feasible under \(K^\star\).  For a nonfactual row, set
\[
 a(y)=\min\{q(y),K_t(y\mid x)/p_t\},
 \qquad d_0=1-\sum_y a(y).
\]
The cap inequalities for \(q\), the rowwise bound \(\delta(K,K^\star)<\rho\), and \(p_t>\kappa\) imply
\[
 d_0
 \le \frac{|p_t-1/2|+
 \|K_t(\cdot\mid x)-(1/2,1/2)\|_1}{p_t}
 <\frac{2\rho}{\kappa}.
\]
The unused caps have total capacity at least \(d_0\), so redistributing this removed mass produces a row feasible under \(K\) at total-variation distance less than \(2\rho/\kappa\).  The factual rows agree at \(\delta_0\).  Reversing \(K\) and \(K^\star\) gives the opposite Hausdorff direction.  Sequential maximal coupling over two transitions therefore moves the infimum or supremum of any fixed center-reward coalition return by at most \(4\rho/\kappa\).  The reward-policy comparison just proved adds \(3\rho\).  Each endpoint in \(\texttt{def:independent-coalition-outer-bound}\) has total absolute Shapley coefficient two, so it moves by at most
\[
 2\left(\frac{4\rho}{\kappa}+3\rho\right)=A.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \min\{\Delta_1^-(\theta),\Delta_1^+(\theta)\}
 \ge \frac{189}{512}-2A
 =\frac{183}{512}-\frac{16}{511}
 >\frac14,
\]
where the last inequality is equivalent to \(55\cdot511>16\cdot512\).

It remains to verify the probability and variance certificates.  Every coordinate difference is bounded by its rowwise \(\ell^1\) distance.  Hence
\[
 \mu_\tau(\theta)
 >\left(\frac{63}{64}-\rho\right)^2
   \left(\frac12-\rho\right)^2>\frac15,
\]
the final rational inequality following, for example, from \(63/64-\rho>49/50\), \(1/2-\rho>49/100\), and \((49/50)^2(49/100)^2>1/5\).  The smallest center policy cell is \(1/64\), and every center transition cell is \(1/2\), so
\[
 s_\pi(\theta)>\frac1{64}-\rho=\frac{15}{1024}>\frac1{100},
 \qquad
 s_K(\theta)>\frac12-\rho=\frac{511}{1024}>\frac25.
\]
For any time-two row write \(a=K_2(1\mid x)\).  Then \(|a-1/2|<\rho\), while the perturbed reward contrast obeys
\[
 |r_2(x,1)-r_2(x,0)|>1-2\rho.
\]
The binary variance identity gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{Y\sim K_2(\cdot\mid x)}\{r_2(x,Y)\}
 =a(1-a)\{r_2(x,1)-r_2(x,0)\}^2
 >\left(\frac14-\rho^2\right)(1-2\rho)^2.
\]
Here \(1/4-\rho^2>6/25\) and \((1-2\rho)^2=(511/512)^2>5/6\), so the product exceeds \(1/5\).  Taking the minimum over \(x\) proves the claimed bound on \(V_{\mathrm{fd}}\).

Finally, the strict metric ball is relative-open in the finite product of valid probability simplices and Euclidean reward cells.  Every probability cell of \(\theta^\star\) is strictly positive, and no continuous coordinate is fixed by the definition of the ball.  Thus all continuous primitives can be perturbed, subject only to row normalization, while the proved inequalities hold uniformly.  This establishes every assertion.

sampling_model.design: Fixed rowwise transition sampling with one simultaneous product confidence region; adaptive online visitation is outside the v1 theorem.
sampling_model.units: For each \((t,x)\), the units are \(n_{t,x}\) observed next-state draws from that transition row.
sampling_model.treatment: Coalition interventions switch the known operational policy from \(\alpha_t^0\) to \(\alpha_t^1\); sampling uncertainty concerns transition marginals, not treatment assignment.
sampling_model.overlap: Population conditioning requires \(p_t>0\) at every factual step, and uniform endpoint consistency is stated on \(p_t\ge\kappa\) classes.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each multinomial row \(K_t(\cdot\mid x)\) is estimated by \(\widehat K_t(\cdot\mid x)\); the endpoint is recomputed over the simultaneous transition-law confidence fiber.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Equation 7 defines the state-contingent trajectory intervention; Assumption 3.3 selects one counterfactually independent and resampled law; Theorem 3.7 proves optimal-policy equivalence; and Theorem 4.2 gives a coalition-proposal sample guarantee.  This workflow does not perform the internally defined coalitionwise ambiguity optimization and is not refuted here.

Under compactness, continuity, and Layer-3 expressivity in Assumption 4.1, Theorem 4.2 gives attained tight bounds by optimizing the whole Shapley functional over one neural-SCM model family.  It does not use the internally defined separate-coalition relaxation and is not refuted here.

Derives exact one-step counterfactual transition bounds and a simultaneous compatible response-law construction; the present paper reuses that row-gluing substrate but studies shared sequential Shapley optimization.
Theorem 2 makes canonical finite-SCM polynomial-program bounds tight for discrete counterfactual probabilities.
Quotienting canonical counterfactual states that are indistinguishable to every LP objective and constraint preserves feasibility and the same sharp bounds.
Quasi-Markovian counterfactual bounds admit tight multilinear programs, with linear programs and polynomial-cardinality exogenous representations in the stated single-intervention setting.
A credal-network mapping gives exact counterfactual bounds on a structural subclass, while exact post-interventional bounding is NP-hard even for polytree-shaped partially specified SCMs.
Proposition 3.2 computes do-Shapley values in time linear in the number of irreducible intervention classes.
Marginal MAP requires sum variables before max variables because the two operators do not commute; this motivates the legal-order constraint but does not itself provide the shared-SCM compiler.
Valid MAP elimination can require exponential constrained width even for polytree networks, consistent with the present active-chain lower boundary.
Iterative split-and-prune circuit transformations preserve and eventually recover an exact marginal-MAP solution.
Theorem 3.1 establishes uniform asymptotic validity for calibrated confidence intervals on partially identified projections.
Ordinary bootstrap consistency can fail for directionally differentiable maps, motivating derivative-aware resampling.
Constructs efficient asymptotically normal estimators for sharp robust dynamic policy-value endpoints.

tldr: Trajectory-conditioned Shapley credit is not point identified by a Markov transition kernel once counterfactual independence across action rows is removed. Each coordinate is the attained interval obtained by optimizing one posterior response-row kernel shared across all coalition worlds. In the complete two-step binary family \(\mathfrak G_{\varepsilon}\), that interval is \([-\varepsilon,\varepsilon/2]\), strictly inside the coalitionwise interval \([-(1+\varepsilon)/2,1/2]\) on an open neighborhood. Exact beta-integral compression replaces the \(2^H\) coalition sum by \(H\) Markov polynomial evaluations, and an explicit reward-range affine lift produces two nonnegative objectives without duplicating row choices. The central open question is a rational constrained-width compiler whose legal sum-before-max order and backpointers retain one shared optimizer and return a compatible endpoint SCM. A simultaneous multinomial confidence fiber covers every coordinate interval on one event, with endpoint error controlled by the smallest factual transition probability.

project_justification.gap: Existing trajectory credit selects counterfactual independence, generic Layer-3 bounds do not exploit Markov structure, and compatible-MDP row bounds do not solve a signed Shapley objective sharing one SCM across coalitions. Existing exact Shapley and marginal-MAP algorithms separately address coalition redundancy or mixed operators, but not their posterior shared-coupling composition.
project_justification.niche: Finite Markov SCMs admit an exact posterior row projection that is far smaller than the canonical response-table simplex, while the Shapley beta integral compresses coalitions before optimization. Their combination creates a structured but nonrectangular mixed-inference problem whose optimizer has a direct causal interpretation.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies attained shared-SCM intervals and witnesses, a fully specified binary strict-gap family with explicit endpoint assignments and open-neighborhood persistence, exact polynomial Shapley compression, a signed-to-nonnegative affine lift, a width-parameterized shared-optimizer compiler question, and whole-set multinomial confidence-fiber inference with a local positivity modulus.

related_work: Li, Lee, and Bareinboim (2026) define the state-contingent trajectory intervention in Equation 7. Their Assumption 3.3 supplies counterfactual independence and resampling, Theorem 3.7 establishes optimal-policy equivalence, and Theorem 4.2 gives the optimal coalition proposal and its sample guarantee; the present interval changes only the unidentified response-row coupling while preserving that destination query and the \(\phi\)-PPO reward and critic consumer. Lee, Plecko, and Bareinboim (2026) establish generic nonidentification and tight neural-SCM optimization for Layer-3 Shapley values; the present paper is informed by that result and seeks explicit shared Markov-row structure rather than a second compactness theorem. Lally, Kazemi, and Paoletti (2026) derive the one-step no-assumption row bounds and simultaneous realization used as identification substrate, but their robust value iteration does not optimize a signed multi-coalition functional and their conclusion leaves estimated-transition uncertainty open. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022) justify restriction to finite canonical response types and tight polynomial programs, while documenting their general computational cost. Witter et al. (2026) compress do-Shapley coalitions using irreducible intervention classes; factual posterior policy-switching worlds do not obey the same fixed intervention equivalence relation. Liu and Ihler (2013) and Park and Darwiche (2004) supply the mixed-inference warning that chance summation cannot be exchanged with response-row maximization and that ordinary treewidth is not the relevant complexity measure. Choi, Friedman, and Van den Broeck (2022) provide a compiler exemplar in which circuit transformations preserve an exact marginal-MAP optimizer. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) motivate confidence-fiber projection, Fang and Santos (2019) rule out a casual bootstrap argument at changing active faces, and Wang (2008) provides the multinomial simultaneous-confidence substrate. Bennett et al. (2024) demonstrate a stronger semiparametric inference rung for sharp dynamic endpoints, which is not claimed here.
technical_internal_limitation: The explicit objectives \(F_i^{+1}\) and \(F_i^{-1}\) have an algebraic nonnegative lift, but their factor-circuit realization and the \(O(H^2Nd^{w_{\mathrm c}+1})\) count have not been independently proved. A correct compiler must use one copy of every \(Z_{t,x}\) within each fixed-sign endpoint circuit across all quadrature, branch, path, and reward selectors; prove the legal elimination invariant; account for global selectors only once per bucket; control rational bit growth; and return a single shared assignment through backpointers. Exhaustive agreement for small binary models is evidence only. If constrained widths show no structured growing-horizon family beyond generic marginal MAP, the computational claim should be downgraded.
honest_scope: The model fixes known deterministic rewards on finite spaces, hence bounded by the derived stagewise extrema, and the operational state-contingent policy interventions in Equation 7 of Li, Lee, and Bareinboim. It varies transition response-table couplings within each time and keeps disturbances independent across time. It does not vary policy response coupling, impose a common response-table law across stages, allow reward-noise coupling, or address hidden global confounders. The population endpoints concern conditional mean credit. They do not sharply identify PTR's root-mean-square priority, its exponential moving average, cross-trajectory priority rankings, or learning performance. The confidence theorem uses fixed rowwise multinomial sampling; adaptive online visitation requires a separate confidence-sequence analysis. Under Assumption 3.3, the distinct set \(\Theta_i^{\mathrm{CI}}(K,\tau)\) equals the published singleton \(\{\Phi_i(q^{\mathrm{CI}})\}\) and is contained in the unrestricted interval \(\Theta_i(K,\tau)\); the unrestricted interval is not asserted to be a singleton.
